Subject: Internal: CloudForge asks — pricing & capacity implications

Internal summary for thread owner (Priyom):

Key commercial impacts from CloudForge's draft:
- 24-month term with mid-term rebaseline: suggest we model two scenarios — (A) 24 months with rebaseline at month 12 where pricing adjusts to actual usage, (B) 24 months with fixed price but option to renegotiate at month 12. Scenario A exposes us to revenue variability; Scenario B gives predictability.
- Reserved 30% burst pool: propose a blended price for reserved capacity + per-token overage. Estimate uplift ~18–22% on baseline unit cost depending on model family.
- Capex/commit vs true reserved capacity: need clarity whether CloudForge expects guaranteed GPU reservation or a billing-only reservation credit.

Action items for pricing and enablement:
- Ben: produce a pricing comparison (A vs B) + seat/capacity uplift impact by EOD Mon (2028-10-30).
- Mina: confirm infra constraints for EU logs and whether reserved pool requires Dedicated vs Hosted routing; list any latency/throughput implications.
- Marissa: legal redline review due Tue.

I'll draft a one-pager with the two pricing scenarios and recommended default. Priyom — I'll loop this into the Nov 1 alignment call draft.

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Oct 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood legal notes on CloudForge redline (high level)

Team — I've reviewed CloudForge_MSA_2028_redline.docx and pulled the items that require negotiation. High-level notes below; I'll produce a tracked-counter by EOD Tue (2028-10-31). Please review and flag any commercial trade-offs.

Top issues:
1) Indemnity and insurance: CloudForge proposes a $5M cap tied to their insurance schedule. We can accept a lower cap but need to preserve carveouts for willful misconduct and IP claims. Ask: confirm policy limits; propose $3M with carveouts.
2) Data residency & logs: acceptable to provide EU residency for logs if they sign a data processing addendum and accept additional fees for cross-region storage. Need Mina to confirm technical feasibility and any export controls.
3) SLA credits: CloudForge tightened credit caps and removed some exclusions. Maintain current cap (20% of month fees) with clearer incident classification. Also push for an annual uptime SLO rather than monthly for complex multi-region routing.
4) Term rebaseline mechanics: CloudForge wording implies unilateral rebaseline — cannot accept. Propose a cooperative rebaseline where both parties agree to any pricing change with defined arbitration step if disagreement.
5) Reserved pool vs capacity guarantee language: clarify whether reserved pool is billed as committed capacity (we invoice reserved portion) or as a credit against burst usage. Prefer invoiced reserved pool to avoid stranded capacity.

Attachments referenced: internal redline checklist (not attached in this thread — will post to Drive)

I'll circulate our tracked redline and a short negotiation playbook (non-starters vs concessions) tomorrow. If procurement needs a legal walkthrough before Nov 10, I can join the call.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
